Let's reconsider the question carefully.

The question is: "What happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day?"

The options are:

A. Nothing happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day.  
B. You will be unlucky for the rest of the year.  
C. You will be lucky for the rest of the year.  
D. You will sweep out all of the good luck.

In many traditional beliefs, especially in some East Asian cultures, cleaning on New Year's Day is thought to sweep away good luck and fortune, which is why people avoid cleaning on that day. This superstition suggests that cleaning on New Year's Day can cause you to lose good luck.

Option D says "You will sweep out all of the good luck," which directly reflects this belief.

Option B says "You will be unlucky for the rest of the year," which is a consequence of sweeping out good luck, but less specific.

Option C says "You will be lucky," which contradicts the superstition.

Option A says "Nothing happens," which ignores the superstition.

Therefore, the most accurate answer reflecting the common superstition is D.

Answer: D
